cases.question: What happens if a team uses an Aggregated Standard Traded Player Exception in a trade that would put Apron Team Salary over the Second Apron Level?

claims.text: The Transaction Restrictions Table assigns the Second Apron Level as the Applicable Apron Level for a team acquiring a player using an Aggregated Standard Traded Player Exception (Section 6(j)(1)(ii)).
claims.quote:
H. Team acquires a player using an Aggregated 
Standard Traded Player Exception (as described 
in Section 6(j)(1)(ii) below) 
Second Apron 
Level

claims.text: Because that transaction carries the Second Apron Level, the trade is prohibited: a team may not engage in a Transaction Restrictions Table transaction if, immediately following it, the team's Apron Team Salary for that Salary Cap Year would exceed the Applicable Apron Level corresponding to the transaction.
claims.quote:
A Team may not engage in a transaction set forth in 
the Transaction Restrictions Table if, immediately 
following such transaction, the Team’s Apron Team 
Salary for such Salary Cap Year would exceed the 
“Applicable Apron Level ” that corresponds with 
such transaction in the table

claims.text: The CBA's own example confirms this: Team D's proposed trade using the Aggregated Standard Traded Player Exception, which would have left a 2024-25 Apron Team Salary of $195 million, is prohibited because that figure exceeds the $189.5 million 2024-25 Second Apron Level.
claims.quote:
Team  D seeks to acquire by 
trade a player using the Aggregated Standard Traded Player Exception.  
Immediately following such trade, Team D’s 2024-25 Apron Team Salary 
would be $195 million.  The proposed trade (a transaction set forth in 
row H of the Transaction Restrictions Table with an Applicable Apron 
Level of the Second Apron Level) is prohibited by Section  2(e)(2)(i)(A) 
above because, immediately following the trade, Team D’s 2024-25 Apron 
Team Salary would exceed $189.5  million (i.e., the 2024-25 Second 
Apron Level).

claims.text: In addition, a team that engages in such a transaction may not, for the remainder of that Salary Cap Year, have an Apron Team Salary exceeding the Applicable Apron Level (here, the Second Apron Level) corresponding to the transaction.
claims.quote:
A Team that engages in a transaction set forth in the 
Transaction Restrictions Table may not, for the 
remainder of such Salary Cap Year, have an Apron 
Team Salary that exceeds the Applicable Apron 
Level that corresponds with such transaction in the 
table.

cases.question: When is a player still eligible for NBA Most Valuable Player if he did not play sixty-five Regular Season games?

claims.text: A player who did not play 65 Regular Season games is still eligible for NBA Most Valuable Player if he satisfies the alternative criterion: he played in at least 62 Regular Season games, suffered a "season-ending injury," and played in at least 85% of the Regular Season games played by his Team prior to suffering that injury.
claims.quote: or (2) the player (A) played in at least sixty-two (62) Regular Season games, (B) suffered a “season-ending injury” (as defined below), and (C) played in at least eighty-five percent (85%) of the Regular Season games played by his Team prior to the player suffering such injury.

claims.text: For that alternative criterion, a "season-ending injury" is an injury that, in the opinion of a physician jointly selected by the NBA and Players Association, makes it substantially more likely than not that the player would be unable to play through the May 31 following the date of the injury.
claims.quote: A “season-ending injury” is an injury that, in the opinion of a physician jointly selected by the NBA and Players Association, makes it substantially more likely than not that the player would be unable to play through the May 31 following the date of such injury

claims.text: A player who fails to satisfy the Award Eligibility Criteria in a Season may nonetheless be deemed eligible for the honors (including MVP) if he prevails in either an Award Eligibility Grievance or an Extraordinary Circumstances Challenge for that Season; he may not bring both in the same Season.
claims.quote: A player who fails to satisfy the Award Eligibility Criteria in a Season may nonetheless be deemed eligible for the Applicable Generally Recognized League Honors if he prevails in either an Award Eligibility Grievance or an Extraordinary Circumstances Challenge in respect of such Season in accordance with the procedures set forth in Sections 6(b) and 6(c) below.

claims.text: In counting games toward these thresholds, a player is considered to have played in a Regular Season game if he played at least 20 minutes of that game, and for no more than two Regular Season games per Season he is considered to have played if he played at least 15 but fewer than 20 minutes.
claims.quote: A player shall be considered to have played in a Regular Season game if he played at least twenty (20) minutes of such game, provided that in respect of no more than two (2) Regular Season games per Season, such player will be considered to have played in a Regular Season game if he played at least fifteen (15) minutes and fewer than twenty (20) minutes in such game.

claims.text: To prevail in an Award Eligibility Grievance, the player must prove by clear and convincing evidence that his Team willfully limited his minutes or games with the intention of depriving him of award eligibility; the sole remedy is that he is deemed eligible.
claims.quote: the player bears the burden of proving, by clear and convincing evidence, that the Team willfully limited the player’s number of minutes played or games played during the Regular Season with the intention of depriving the player of eligibility for one or more of the Applicable Generally Recognized League Honors for such Season.

claims.text: To prevail in an Extraordinary Circumstances Challenge, the player must prove that extraordinary circumstances made it impracticable for him to play in one or more missed Regular Season games, that he would have satisfied the 65-game criterion had he played every game missed due to those circumstances (assuming 20 minutes in each such game), and that, in the totality of the circumstances, it would be unjust to exclude him from eligibility.
claims.quote: Due to extraordinary circumstances, it was  impracticable for him to play in one (1) or more of the Regular Season game(s) that he missed during such Season;

cases.question: How does the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception change above the Second Apron Level, and which transaction table covers that limit?

claims.text: The limit on the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception is set by the Transaction Restrictions Table in Section 2(e)(4). That table lists the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception in row K, and the Applicable Apron Level corresponding to that row is the Second Apron Level. So the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception is capped at — and cannot be used to go above — the Second Apron Level.
claims.quote:
K. Team signs a player using the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception (as described in  
Section 6(f) below) 
Second Apron 
Level

claims.text: Mechanically, the table operates as a bar: a team may not engage in a listed transaction if, immediately following the transaction, its Apron Team Salary would exceed the Applicable Apron Level tied to that transaction — for a row K Taxpayer Mid-Level signing, that is the Second Apron Level.
claims.quote:
(A) A Team may not engage in a transaction set forth in the 
Transaction Restrictions Table if, immediately following such 
transaction, the Team’s Apron Team Salary for such Salary Cap 
Year would exceed the “Applicable Apron Level ” that corresponds with 
such transaction in the table; and

claims.text: Once a team uses the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception, it may not, for the remainder of that Salary Cap Year, have an Apron Team Salary exceeding the Second Apron Level — the Applicable Apron Level corresponding to row K.
claims.quote:
(B) A Team that engages in a transaction set forth in the 
Transaction Restrictions Table may not, for the 
remainder of such Salary Cap Year, have an Apron Team Salary that exceeds the Applicable Apron 
Level that corresponds with such transaction in the 
table.

claims.text: Above the Second Apron Level the change is a hard restriction on other transactions: during the 2023-24 Salary Cap Year, a team that has signed a Player Contract using the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception may not engage in any transaction in rows A through E of the Transaction Restrictions Table.
claims.quote:
(A) During the 2023-24 Salary Cap Year, a Team may 
not engage in any transaction set forth in rows A 
through E of the Transaction Restrictions Table if it 
has previously signed a Player Contract pursuant to 
the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception during 
such Salary Cap Year.

claims.text: For each Salary Cap Year beginning with 2024-25, that freeze extends one row further: a team that has previously signed a Player Contract under the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception in that Salary Cap Year may not engage in any transaction in rows A through F of the Transaction Restrictions Table.
claims.quote:
(B) For ea ch Salary Cap Year beginning with the 
2024-25 Salary Cap Year, a Team may not engage in 
any transaction set forth in rows A through F of the 
Transaction Restrictions Table  if it has previously 
signed a Player Contract pursuant to the Taxpayer 
Mid-Level Salary Exception during such Salary Cap 
Year.

claims.text: The exception itself is conditioned on being above the First Apron Level: a team may use the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception only if its Apron Team Salary immediately following use of the exception exceeds the First Apron Level, which is why use of the exception pushes the team's applicable ceiling to the Second Apron Level in row K.

cases.question: What counts toward the cap as Salary, and how is Team Salary determined?

claims.text: “Salary” is defined, for a Salary Cap Year, as a player’s Compensation with respect to the Season covered by that Salary Cap Year, plus any other amount deemed to constitute Salary under the Agreement. It excludes Unlikely Bonuses, benefits received under the Agreement (such as Article IV benefits, per diem, and moving expenses), and any portion of Compensation attributable to another Salary Cap Year; it also includes any consideration received by a retired player that is deemed Salary under Article XIII.
claims.quote:
(lll) “Salary” means, with respect to a Salary Cap Year, a player’s 
Compensation with respect to the Season covered by such Salary Cap Year, 
plus any other amount that is deemed to constitute Salary in accordance with 
the terms of this Agreement, not including Unlikely Bonuses, any benefits 
the player received in accordanc e with the terms of this Agreement 
(including, e.g., the benefits provided for by Article IV, per diem, and moving 
expenses), and any portion of the player’s Compensation that is attributable 
to another Salary Cap Year in accordance with this Agreement.

claims.text: “Team Salary” for a Salary Cap Year is the sum of all Salaries attributable to a Team’s active and former players plus other amounts computed under Article VII, less applicable credit amounts computed under Article VII.

of all Salaries attributable to a Team’s active and former players pl us other 
amounts as computed in accordance with Article  VII, less applicable credit 
amounts as computed in accordance with Article VII.

cases.question: An Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agent has a prior regular salary of 10000000 and the prior average player salary is 12000000. What is the first-year cap under the veteran free agent exception?

claims.text: For an Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agent, the Veteran Free Agent Exception lets the new contract provide, in the first Salary Cap Year, up to the greater of (A) 175% of the Regular Salary for the final Salary Cap Year of the prior contract (plus 175% of any Likely and Unlikely Bonuses) or (B) 105% of the Average Player Salary for the prior Salary Cap Year. Applying (A): 175% × $10,000,000 = $17,500,000.
claims.quote: (A) one hundred seventy-five percent (175%) of the Regular Salary for the final Salary Cap Year covered by his prior Contract

claims.text: Applying the alternative in (B): 105% × $12,000,000 = $12,600,000. Because $17,500,000 (the 175% figure) is greater than $12,600,000, the first-year amount permitted under the Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agent exception is $17,500,000 (subject to Article II, Section 7).
claims.quote: (B) Salary plus Unlikely Bonuses totaling an amount equal to one hundred five percent (105%) of the Average Player Salary for the prior Salary Cap Year

claims.text: A Second Apron Team is prohibited from trading (conditionally or unconditionally) its first round draft pick in the first NBA Draft that occurs following the seventh Season that follows the Season occurring within that Salary Cap Year.
